question:
(i) Explain why one coulomb is considered a large unit of charge in electrostatics.
(ii) Estimate the number of electrons constituting a charge of $-1\,\text{C}$. Take $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.

options.A:
(i) One coulomb is a small charge because it contains only one electron
(ii) $-1\,\text{C}$ corresponds to $6.25\times10^{-19}$ electrons
options.B:
(i) One coulomb is large because it contains a very large number of elementary charges and produces strong electrostatic forces
(ii) $-1\,\text{C}$ corresponds to about $6.25\times10^{18}$ excess electrons
options.C:
(i) One coulomb is large because protons are infinitely massive
(ii) $-1\,\text{C}$ corresponds to $1.6\times10^{-19}$ electrons
options.D:
(i) One coulomb is large only because it is measured in SI units
(ii) $-1\,\text{C}$ corresponds to $1.6\times10^{19}$ deficient electrons
